Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier. Resets every path test.patch touches to the immutable harbor_base tag, applies
# the hidden tests, runs ONLY the configured f2p + p2p tests with the repository's own runner into a
# JUnit report, and lets verifier.py turn that report into the reward. Nothing here reads the
# candidate's source to decide anything.
set -uo pipefail

# ---- task-specific values, filled by the task builder ----------------------------------------
# run_tests runs the configured tests with the repository's own runner and writes JUnit XML to
# $JUNIT_OUT. The test ids (f2p + p2p from /tests/config.json) are in $TEST_IDS_FILE, one per line.
# Write plain shell commands here; no quoting of the whole block is needed.
run_tests() {
  npx vitest run \
    examples/toolbar-active-id-disabled/test.ts \
    examples/toolbar-active-id-stale/test.ts \
    examples/composite/test.ts \
    examples/toolbar/test.ts \
    examples/tab/test.ts \
    examples/radio/test.ts \
    --reporter=junit --outputFile="$JUNIT_OUT"
}
# Directories holding the repo's test plumbing (configs, helpers) that must also be restored so a
# candidate cannot replace the harness. Space-separated, relative to /app; '' if none.
PROTECTED_DIRS='examples/composite/test.ts examples/toolbar/test.ts examples/tab/test.ts examples/radio/test.ts vitest.config.ts vitest.setup.ts package.json'
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
export JUNIT_OUT=/logs/verifier/junit.xml
export TEST_IDS_FILE=/logs/verifier/test_ids.txt
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"
rm -f "$JUNIT_OUT" /logs/verifier/reward.txt /logs/verifier/reward.json

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# Capture the agent's submission BEFORE anything below mutates /app -- this is the last
# moment the tree is base + agent work; the restore loop and test.patch come next.
#
# A THROWAWAY INDEX, never /app/.git/index: `git add` against the real one would leave paths
# staged and change how the `git checkout harbor_base --` and `git clean` below behave.
#
# TRACKED EDITS + A SOURCE WHITELIST, not `add -A` with a blacklist. This image builds wx
# in-tree AFTER the harbor_base commit (environment/Dockerfile), so everything the build
# emits is untracked and NOT in wx's .gitignore. A bare `add -A` captured 380MB of .o/.d/.so;
# excluding those by extension still left ~120 configure-generated files (samples/*/Makefile,
# bk-deps, version-script, lib/wx/config/*, the utils/wxrc/wxrc binary) because most have no
# extension to blacklist. Inverting it -- stage tracked modifications, then add only untracked
# files that LOOK like source -- keeps the agent's work and drops generated output by default.
_SUB=/logs/verifier/submission.patch
_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'
         '*.py' '*.rb' '*.go' '*.rs' '*.java' '*.js' '*.ts' '*.tsx' '*.cs' '*.kt' '*.swift')
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app read-tree harbor_base 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
# Enumerate before adding: `git add` aborts and stages NOTHING if any one pathspec matches
# no file, which silently drops the agent's new files on most tasks.
# Generated-output dirs are dropped from the UNTRACKED scan only. A project that keeps real
# source under lib/ is unaffected: those files are tracked at harbor_base, so `add -u` above
# already has them. This drops only files CREATED under a build dir during the run -- which,
# left in, break replay: they are recorded as new-file hunks and a fresh container from the
# same image already has them, so `git apply` fails with "already exists in working directory".
mapfile -t _SUBNEW < <(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard \
  -- "${_SUBSRC[@]}" ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' 2>/dev/null)
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
  GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -- "${_SUBNEW[@]}" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
fi
GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app diff --binary --cached harbor_base \
  > "$_SUB" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true
rm -f "$_SUBIDX"

# WHAT THE WHITELIST DROPPED, listed rather than silently discarded. The split above captures
# every change to a TRACKED file (any extension, deletions included) but only NEW files that
# look like source -- so an agent adding config.yml, a .cmake module or an extensionless script
# loses it, and the patch still looks clean. That is the failure this manifest exists to expose.
#
# NEWEST FIRST, which is the useful ordering and not a cosmetic one: build output and image
# assets are created before the agent phase starts, so anything the agent made sorts to the top.
# Build artifacts are excluded by the same rules as the capture, to keep the list readable.
#
# If something here belongs in the submission, widen _SUBSRC. Do not reach for `add -A`.
_SUBSKIP=/logs/verifier/submission-skipped.txt
_SUBCAP=/tmp/.submission_captured
if [ "${#_SUBNEW[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then printf '%s\n' "${_SUBNEW[@]}" > "$_SUBCAP"; else : > "$_SUBCAP"; fi
_SUBSKIPN=$(git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
    ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
    ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
    ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
  | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
{ echo "# Untracked files NOT captured into submission.patch, newest first."
  echo "# Anything the agent created sorts above build output, which predates the agent phase."
  echo "# total: ${_SUBSKIPN}  (showing at most 40)"
  git -C /app ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- . \
      ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
      ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
      ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -vxF -f "$_SUBCAP" 2>/dev/null | head -200 \
    | while IFS= read -r _f; do
        printf '%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$(stat -c %Y "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" \
                              "$(stat -c %s "/app/$_f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)" "$_f"
      done \
    | sort -rn | head -40 | awk -F'\t' '{printf "%s\t%s\t%s\n",$1,$2,$3}'
} > "$_SUBSKIP" 2>/dev/null || true
rm -f "$_SUBCAP"

# Size guard. The whitelist is a heuristic, so a task laying out source unusually could still
# produce something enormous. Cap it and leave a diagnosable stub: a truncated capture is
# recoverable, a full disk is not.
_SUBSZ=$(wc -c < "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
if [ "$_SUBSZ" -gt 5242880 ]; then
  { echo "SUBMISSION CAPTURE SUPPRESSED: ${_SUBSZ} bytes exceeds the 5MB cap."
    echo "Directories contributing to the discarded patch:"
    grep -a "^diff --git" "$_SUB" | sed 's#^diff --git a/##; s# b/.*##; s#/[^/]*$##' \
      | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
  } > "$_SUB.suppressed" 2>/dev/null
  : > "$_SUB"
  echo "== submission.patch SUPPRESSED (${_SUBSZ} bytes > 5MB cap) ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
else
  echo "== captured submission.patch (${_SUBSZ} bytes, $(grep -ac '^diff --git' "$_SUB" 2>/dev/null || echo 0) files) ==" \
    | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
fi


# 1. Restore every path test.patch touches. Both diff headers are read, so new files, binary
#    baselines (image-comparison PNGs, snapshots), renames and deletions are all covered.
_patch_paths=$( { sed -n 's#^diff --git a/\(.*\) b/.*#\1#p' /tests/test.patch
                  sed -n 's#^diff --git a/.* b/\(.*\)#\1#p' /tests/test.patch; } | sort -u )
for _p in $_patch_paths; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_p" 2>/dev/null || rm -rf "/app/$_p" 2>/dev/null || true
done
for _d in $PROTECTED_DIRS; do
  git -C /app checkout harbor_base -- "$_d" 2>/dev/null || true
  git -C /app clean -fdq -- "$_d" 2>/dev/null || true
done

# 2. Apply the hidden tests.
echo "== applying test.patch ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
git apply --binary /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || git apply /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || patch -p1 -i /tests/test.patch 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || { echo "ERROR: could not apply test.patch" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# 3. Run only the configured tests.
python3 - <<'PY' > "$TEST_IDS_FILE"
import json
c = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
print("\n".join(c["f2p"] + c["p2p"]))
PY
echo "== running f2p + p2p tests ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
( cd /app && run_tests ) >>"$STDOUT_LOG" 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" \
  || echo "(tests exited non-zero; parsing the report)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

# 4. Reward from the report.
echo "== computing reward ==" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"
# Rubric judge — SUB-AGENT backend: no API key, no network. On the first pass there is no
# verdict yet, so judge.py writes a judge request under /logs/verifier/judge/ and prints
# nothing; scoring falls back to tests alone. Once a judge sub-agent has written
# verdict.json there, `mm_run.sh <task> rescore` folds the verdict into the reward.
# The `|| echo ""` is load-bearing: the judge must never be able to fail the run.
RUBRIC=""
if [ -f /tests/rubrics.json ]; then
  RUBRIC=$(python3 /tests/judge.py --rubrics /tests/rubrics.json --repo /app \
             2>/logs/verifier/judge.log || echo "")
  echo "Rubric verdict: ${RUBRIC:-pending (judge request written; rescore after grading)}"
fi

python3 /tests/verifier.py "${REPORTS[@]}" --rubric "${RUBRIC:-}"

echo "reward=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null)" | tee -a "$STDOUT_LOG"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the JUnit report into the task reward.

The reward is binary: 1.0 only when every configured f2p and p2p test is found exactly once in the
report and passed; otherwise 0.0. f2p_passed / f2p_total and p2p_passed / p2p_total record how close
a run came. The verifier reads test outcomes only, never the candidate's source.
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import json as _cj, os as _co, sys as _cs

_CANON_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"
_CANON_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy for the whole corpus. BINARY -- there is no partial credit.

    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes. A
    strict subset of f2p passing is not partial progress worth scoring: the task is unsolved,
    so it is 0.0.

    reward is the same value, zeroed when the rubric judge failed a criterion. A "pass" or a
    "not graded" verdict never lowers the score -- the judge must never be able to penalise a
    run it could not grade.
    """
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon["reward"]


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        _co.makedirs(_co.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, "w") as _h:
            _cj.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)
        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script and the
        # lighthouse UI read reward.txt. Writing both from one dict means they cannot disagree.
        with open(_CANON_TXT, "w") as _h:
            _h.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as _exc:
        print("WARNING: could not write %s: %s" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=_cs.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.

    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail -- including the empty string test.sh passes
    when judge.py wrote no verdict -- means "not graded", which must never penalise the run.
    """
    if "--rubric" not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index("--rubric")
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ""
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


CONF = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P, P2P = CONF["f2p"], CONF["p2p"]
REPORT = os.environ.get("JUNIT_OUT", "/logs/verifier/junit.xml")
OUT_DIR = "/logs/verifier"


def load_junit(path):
    """Every reported test, keyed by "classname name" and by name; a key seen twice with different
    outcomes counts as failed."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return results
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
        outcome = "skip" if "skipped" in tags else ("fail" if tags & {"failure", "error"} else "pass")
        full = f"{tc.get('classname', '')} {tc.get('name', '')}".strip()
        for key in {full, tc.get("name", "")}:
            if key in results and results[key] != outcome:
                results[key] = "fail"
            else:
                results[key] = outcome
    return results


def junit_key(test_id):
    """A pytest node id (tests/test_x.py::TestA::test_b[png]) as the JUnit report names it
    ("tests.test_x.TestA test_b[png]"); other ids unchanged."""
    if "::" not in test_id:
        return test_id
    parts = test_id.split("::")
    mod = parts[0][:-3] if parts[0].endswith(".py") else parts[0]
    return f"{'.'.join([mod.replace('/', '.')] + parts[1:-1])} {parts[-1]}"


def resolve(test_id, results):
    """The outcome of one configured test: an exact key match first (the id as written, or a
    pytest node id in JUnit form), else the single reported test whose key ends with it. Missing
    or ambiguous counts as not passed."""
    keys = [test_id, junit_key(test_id)]
    if " > " in test_id:  # "describe > test": jest-junit joins with a space, playwright with " › "
        head, rest = test_id.split(" > ", 1)
        keys += [test_id.replace(" > ", " "), test_id.replace(" > ", " › "), head + " " + rest.replace(" > ", " › ")]
    keys += [k.replace('"', "") for k in keys]  # jest-junit drops quotation marks from names
    keys = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    for key in keys:
        if key in results:
            return results[key]
    for key in keys:
        hits = {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k.endswith(key)}
        if hits and len(set(hits.values())) == 1:
            return next(iter(hits.values()))
        if hits:
            return "ambiguous"
    # "file > test" with a describe level left out: a test in that file whose name ends the same
    parts = test_id.split(" > ")
    if len(parts) >= 2 and ("." in parts[0] or "/" in parts[0]):
        hits = {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k.startswith(parts[0] + " ") and k.endswith(parts[-1])}
        if hits and len(set(hits.values())) == 1:
            return next(iter(hits.values()))
        if hits:
            return "ambiguous"
    return "missing"


def main():
    results = load_junit(REPORT)
    detail = {}
    f2p_ok = 0
    for t in F2P:
        r = resolve(t, results)
        detail[f"f2p::{t}"] = r
        f2p_ok += r == "pass"
    p2p_ok = 0
    for t in P2P:
        r = resolve(t, results)
        detail[f"p2p::{t}"] = r
        p2p_ok += r == "pass"
    canon_reward(f2p_ok, len(F2P), p2p_ok, len(P2P), ru

tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). #!/usr/bin/env bash
# Behavioral verifier. Resets every path test.patch touches to the immutable harbor_base tag, applies
# the hidden tests, runs ONLY the configured f2p + p2p tests with the repository's own runner into a
# JUnit report, and lets verifier.py turn that report into the reward. Nothing here reads the
# candidate's source to decide anything.
set -uo pipefail

# ---- task-specific values, filled by the task builder ----------------------------------------
# run_tests runs the configured tests with the repository's own runner and writes JUnit XML to
# $JUNIT_OUT. The test ids (f2p + p2p from /tests/config.json) are in $TEST_IDS_FILE, one per line.
# Write plain shell commands here; no quoting of the whole block is needed.
run_tests() {
  npx vitest run \
    examples/toolbar-active-id-disabled/test.ts \
    examples/toolbar-active-id-stale/test.ts \
    examples/composite/test.ts \
    examples/toolbar/test.ts \
    examples/tab/test.ts \
    examples/radio/test.ts \
    --reporter=junit --outputFile="$JUNIT_OUT"
}
# Directories holding the repo's test plumbing (configs, helpers) that must also be restored so a
# candidate cannot replace the harness. Space-separated, relative to /app; '' if none.
PROTECTED_DIRS='examples/composite/test.ts examples/toolbar/test.ts examples/tab/test.ts examples/radio/test.ts vitest.config.ts vitest.setup.ts package.json'
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

mkdir -p /logs/verifier
STDOUT_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stdout.txt
STDERR_LOG=/logs/verifier/test-stderr.txt
export JUNIT_OUT=/logs/verifier/junit.xml
export TEST_IDS_FILE=/logs/verifier/test_ids.txt
: > "$STDOUT_LOG"; : > "$STDERR_LOG"
rm -f "$JUNIT_OUT" /logs/verifier/reward.txt /logs/verifier/reward.json

ensure_reward() { [ -f /logs/verifier/reward.txt ] || echo 0 > /logs/verifier/reward.txt; }
trap ensure_reward EXIT

cd /app || { echo "no /app" | tee -a "$STDERR_LOG"; exit 1; }

# Capture the agent's submission BEFORE anything below mutates /app -- this is the last
# moment the tree is base + agent work; the restore loop and test.patch come next.
#
# A THROWAWAY INDEX, never /app/.git/index: `git add` against the real one would leave paths
# staged and change how the `git checkout harbor_base --` and `git clean` below behave.
#
# TRACKED EDITS + A SOURCE WHITELIST, not `add -A` with a blacklist. This image builds wx

_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index
_SUBSRC=('*.c' '*.cc' '*.cpp' '*.cxx' '*.h' '*.hh' '*.hpp' '*.hxx' '*.inl' '*.m' '*.mm'

GIT_INDEX_FILE="$_SUBIDX" git -C /app add -u 2>>"$STDERR_LOG" || true

# Generated-output dirs are dropped from the UNTRACKED scan only. A project that keeps real
# source under lib/ is unaffected: those files are tracked at harbor_base, so `add -u` above
# already has them. This drops only files CREATED under a build dir during the run -- which,
# left in, break replay: they are recorded as new-file hunks and a fresh container from the

  -- "${_SUBSRC[@]}" ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' 2>/dev/null)

    ':(exclude)lib/' ':(exclude)build/' ':(exclude).deps/' \
    ':(exclude)*.o' ':(exclude)*.d' ':(exclude)*.a' ':(exclude)*.lo' ':(exclude)*.la' \
    ':(exclude)*.so' ':(exclude)*.so.*' ':(exclude)*.gch' ':(exclude)*.pyc' 2>/dev/null \

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the JUnit report into the task reward.

The reward is binary: 1.0 only when every configured f2p and p2p test is found exactly once in the
report and passed; otherwise 0.0. f2p_passed / f2p_total and p2p_passed / p2p_total record how close
a run came. The verifier reads test outcomes only, never the candidate's source.
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import json as _cj, os as _co, sys as _cs

_CANON_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"
_CANON_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy for the whole corpus. BINARY -- there is no partial credit.

    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes. A
    strict subset of f2p passing is not partial progress worth scoring: the task is unsolved,
    so it is 0.0.

    reward is the same value, zeroed when the rubric judge failed a criterion. A "pass" or a
    "not graded" verdict never lowers the score -- the judge must never be able to penalise a
    run it could not grade.
    """
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon["reward"]


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        _co.makedirs(_co.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, "w") as _h:
            _cj.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)
        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script and the
        # lighthouse UI read reward.txt. Writing both from one dict means they cannot disagree.
        with open(_CANON_TXT, "w") as _h:
            _h.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as _exc:
        print("WARNING: could not write %s: %s" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=_cs.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.

    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail -- including the empty string test.sh passes
    when judge.py wrote no verdict -- means "not graded", which must never penalise the run.
    """
    if "--rubric" not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index("--rubric")
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ""
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


CONF = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P, P2P = CONF["f2p"], CONF["p2p"]
REPORT = os.environ.get("JUNIT_OUT", "/logs/verifier/junit.xml")
OUT_DIR = "/logs/verifier"


def load_junit(path):
    """Every reported test, keyed by "classname name" and by name; a key seen twice with different
    outcomes counts as failed."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return results
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
        outcome = "skip" if "skipped" in tags else ("fail" if tags & {"failure", "error"} else "pass")
        full = f"{tc.get('classname', '')} {tc.get('name', '')}".strip()
        for key in {full, tc.get("name", "")}:
            if key in results and results[key] != outcome:
                results[key] = "fail"
            else:
                results[key] = outcome
    return results


def junit_key(test_id):
    """A pytest node id (tests/test_x.py::TestA::test_b[png]) as the JUnit report names it
    ("tests.test_x.TestA test_b[png]"); other ids unchanged."""
    if "::" not in test_id:
        return test_id
    parts = test_id.split("::")
    mod = parts[0][:-3] if parts[0].endswith(".py") else parts[0]
    return f"{'.'.join([mod.replace('/', '.')] + parts[1:-1])} {parts[-1]}"


def resolve(test_id, results):
    """The outcome of one configured test: an exact key match first (the id as written, or a
    pytest node id in JUnit form), else the single reported test whose key ends with it. Missing
    or ambiguous counts as not passed."""
    keys = [test_id, junit_key(test_id)]
    if " > " in test_id:  # "describe > test": jest-junit joins with a space, playwright with " › "
        head, rest = test_id.split(" > ", 1)
        keys += [test_id.replace(" > ", " "), test_id.replace(" > ", " › "), head + " " + rest.replace(" > ", " › ")]
    keys += [k.replace('"', "") for k in keys]  # jest-junit drops quotation marks from names
    keys = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    for key in keys:
        if key in results:
            return results[key]
    for key in keys:
        hits = {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k.endswith(key)}
        if hits and len(set(hits.values())) == 1:
            return next(iter(hits.values()))
        if hits:
            return "ambiguous"
    # "file > test" with a describe level left out: a test in that file whose name ends the same
    parts = test_id.split(" > ")
    if len(parts) >= 2 and ("." in parts[0] or "/" in parts[0]):
        hits = {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k.startswith(parts[0] + " ") and k.endswith(parts[-1])}
        if hits and len(set(hits.values())) == 1:
            return next(iter(hits.values()))
        if hits:
            return "ambiguous"
    return "missing"


def main():
    results = load_junit(REPORT)
    detail = {}
    f2p_ok = 0
    for t in F2P:
        r = resolve(t, results)
        detail[f"f2p::{t}"] = r
        f2p_ok += r == "pass"
    p2p_ok = 0
    for t in P2P:
        r = resolve(t, results)
        detail[f"p2p::{t}"] = r
        p2p_ok += r == "pass"
    canon_reward(f2p_ok, len(F2P), p2p_ok, len(P2P), rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))
    reward = dict(_canon)
    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    json.dump(detail, open(f"{OUT_DIR}/reward_detail.json", "w"), indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(reward))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    examples/toolbar-active-id-disabled/test.ts \
    examples/toolbar-active-id-stale/test.ts \

_SUBIDX=/tmp/.submission_index

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Turn the JUnit report into the task reward.

The reward is binary: 1.0 only when every configured f2p and p2p test is found exactly once in the
report and passed; otherwise 0.0. f2p_passed / f2p_total and p2p_passed / p2p_total record how close
a run came. The verifier reads test outcomes only, never the candidate's source.
"""
import atexit
import json
import os
import sys
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET

import json as _cj, os as _co, sys as _cs

_CANON_JSON = "/logs/verifier/reward.json"
_CANON_TXT = "/logs/verifier/reward.txt"
_canon = {}


def canon_reward(f2p_passed, f2p_total, p2p_passed, p2p_total, rubric):
    """THE reward policy for the whole corpus. BINARY -- there is no partial credit.

    tests_passed is 1.0 only when every f2p test passes AND every p2p test still passes. A
    strict subset of f2p passing is not partial progress worth scoring: the task is unsolved,
    so it is 0.0.

    reward is the same value, zeroed when the rubric judge failed a criterion. A "pass" or a
    "not graded" verdict never lowers the score -- the judge must never be able to penalise a
    run it could not grade.
    """
    f, t = int(f2p_passed), int(f2p_total)
    p, q = int(p2p_passed), int(p2p_total)
    solved = bool(t) and f == t and p == q
    tests_passed = 1.0 if solved else 0.0
    _canon.clear()
    _canon.update({
        "reward": 0.0 if rubric == "fail" else tests_passed,
        "tests_passed": tests_passed,
        "f2p_passed": f, "f2p_total": t,
        "p2p_passed": p, "p2p_total": q,
        "rubric_passed": {"pass": 1, "fail": 0}.get(rubric, -1),
    })
    return _canon["reward"]


@atexit.register
def _canon_flush():
    if not _canon:
        return
    try:
        _co.makedirs(_co.path.dirname(_CANON_JSON), exist_ok=True)
        with open(_CANON_JSON, "w") as _h:
            _cj.dump(_canon, _h, indent=2)
        # reward.txt too: harbor prefers reward.json, but the sandbox teardown script and the
        # lighthouse UI read reward.txt. Writing both from one dict means they cannot disagree.
        with open(_CANON_TXT, "w") as _h:
            _h.write(str(_canon["reward"]))
    except Exception as _exc:
        print("WARNING: could not write %s: %s" % (_CANON_JSON, _exc), file=_cs.stderr)


def rubric_verdict(argv):
    """The verdict test.sh hands in as `--rubric pass|fail|""`.

    Anything that is not an explicit pass/fail -- including the empty string test.sh passes
    when judge.py wrote no verdict -- means "not graded", which must never penalise the run.
    """
    if "--rubric" not in argv:
        return None
    i = argv.index("--rubric")
    value = argv[i + 1].strip().lower() if i + 1 < len(argv) else ""
    return value if value in ("pass", "fail") else None


CONF = json.load(open("/tests/config.json"))
F2P, P2P = CONF["f2p"], CONF["p2p"]
REPORT = os.environ.get("JUNIT_OUT", "/logs/verifier/junit.xml")
OUT_DIR = "/logs/verifier"


def load_junit(path):
    """Every reported test, keyed by "classname name" and by name; a key seen twice with different
    outcomes counts as failed."""
    results = {}
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return results
    try:
        root = ET.parse(path).getroot()
    except ET.ParseError:
        return results
    for tc in root.iter("testcase"):
        tags = {c.tag for c in tc}
        outcome = "skip" if "skipped" in tags else ("fail" if tags & {"failure", "error"} else "pass")
        full = f"{tc.get('classname', '')} {tc.get('name', '')}".strip()
        for key in {full, tc.get("name", "")}:
            if key in results and results[key] != outcome:
                results[key] = "fail"
            else:
                results[key] = outcome
    return results


def junit_key(test_id):
    """A pytest node id (tests/test_x.py::TestA::test_b[png]) as the JUnit report names it
    ("tests.test_x.TestA test_b[png]"); other ids unchanged."""
    if "::" not in test_id:
        return test_id
    parts = test_id.split("::")
    mod = parts[0][:-3] if parts[0].endswith(".py") else parts[0]
    return f"{'.'.join([mod.replace('/', '.')] + parts[1:-1])} {parts[-1]}"


def resolve(test_id, results):
    """The outcome of one configured test: an exact key match first (the id as written, or a
    pytest node id in JUnit form), else the single reported test whose key ends with it. Missing
    or ambiguous counts as not passed."""
    keys = [test_id, junit_key(test_id)]
    if " > " in test_id:  # "describe > test": jest-junit joins with a space, playwright with " › "
        head, rest = test_id.split(" > ", 1)
        keys += [test_id.replace(" > ", " "), test_id.replace(" > ", " › "), head + " " + rest.replace(" > ", " › ")]
    keys += [k.replace('"', "") for k in keys]  # jest-junit drops quotation marks from names
    keys = list(dict.fromkeys(keys))
    for key in keys:
        if key in results:
            return results[key]
    for key in keys:
        hits = {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k.endswith(key)}
        if hits and len(set(hits.values())) == 1:
            return next(iter(hits.values()))
        if hits:
            return "ambiguous"
    # "file > test" with a describe level left out: a test in that file whose name ends the same
    parts = test_id.split(" > ")
    if len(parts) >= 2 and ("." in parts[0] or "/" in parts[0]):
        hits = {k: v for k, v in results.items() if k.startswith(parts[0] + " ") and k.endswith(parts[-1])}
        if hits and len(set(hits.values())) == 1:
            return next(iter(hits.values()))
        if hits:
            return "ambiguous"
    return "missing"


def main():
    results = load_junit(REPORT)
    detail = {}
    f2p_ok = 0
    for t in F2P:
        r = resolve(t, results)
        detail[f"f2p::{t}"] = r
        f2p_ok += r == "pass"
    p2p_ok = 0
    for t in P2P:
        r = resolve(t, results)
        detail[f"p2p::{t}"] = r
        p2p_ok += r == "pass"
    canon_reward(f2p_ok, len(F2P), p2p_ok, len(P2P), rubric_verdict(sys.argv[1:]))
    reward = dict(_canon)
    os.makedirs(OUT_DIR, exist_ok=True)
    json.dump(detail, open(f"{OUT_DIR}/reward_detail.json", "w"), indent=2)
    print(json.dumps(reward))


if __name__ == "__main__":
